facts.title: Reunion Announcement Tease (August 27, 2024)
facts.body: On August 27, 2024, Liam and Noel Gallagher both posted teasing messages about an upcoming announcement, prompting widespread anticipation among fans and media outlets like the BBC about a potential Oasis reunion. "Yes, Oasis fans hoping that this morning they will hear the news that they've been waiting for for years that the legendary band are getting back together."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Reunion Confirmed and Stadium Shows Sold Out (August 27, 2024)
facts.body: The reunion was officially confirmed at 8 AM GMT on August 27, 2024. In the subsequent weeks, Oasis sold out 41 stadium shows across the UK, Ireland, North America, Japan, Australia, and South America, with tickets selling out instantly upon release. "And at 8am GMT that day, the rumors were confirmed."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Extensive Planning and Negotiations for Reunion (Pre-2024)
facts.body: A reunion of this scale required extensive planning and negotiation, including the brothers' agreement to reform, completion of existing contractual obligations, drafting of complex legal contracts, securing venues, and identifying merchandise and promotional opportunities, a process estimated to take a year or more. "Well, a reunion of this magnitude takes a lot of planning and negotiation."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Peggy Gallagher's Influence on Reconciliation (Pre-2024)
facts.body: The boys' mother, Peggy Gallagher, was noted as a potential factor in the brothers' reconciliation. As she aged, she was deeply upset by their estrangement, suggesting that making her happy may have played a role in their decision to reunite. "First, there's Peggy Gallagher, the boy's mom. She was getting older and was very broken up, the two of her sons had become such enemies."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Noel Gallagher's Divorce Settlement (Pre-2024)
facts.body: Noel Gallagher's divorce from his longtime partner, Sarah McDonald, after 12 years, cost him at least £20 million and nearly led to the loss of an expensive house. This divorce had to be finalized before any reunion plans could proceed. "Meanwhile, Noel went through a divorce with his longtime partner, Sarah McDonald. They split after 12 years together, something that cost no at least 20 million pounds."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)

facts.title: "HISS" as First Pure Rap Diss to Top Hot 100 (2024)
facts.body: Megan Thee Stallion's "HISS," which debuted at number one in February 2024, became "the first pure rap diss record to top the Hot 100," excluding Timbaland's pop track "Give It To Me." This achievement underscored how streaming had "changed the game," allowing incendiary rap beef to dominate the charts. "When HISS debuted at number one in February 2024, it became the first pure rap diss record to top the hot 100, not counting the aforementioned Timberland pop track Give It To Me from 2007."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: hip hop

facts.body: Kendrick Lamar's "Not Like Us" "changed the game for rap music, for hip-hop culture, and in the history of the diss record." Its unprecedented chart success, Grammy wins, and Super Bowl performance cemented its status as a pivotal moment for the genre. "Not Like Us changed the game for rap music, for hip-hop culture, and in the history of the dis record."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: Adele World Temporary Residency (2024)
facts.body: In 2024, Live Nation constructed a temporary pop-up stadium in Munich capable of holding 80,000 people, creating "Adele World." During this unique residency, Adele performed twice a week for a month, drawing 730,000 attendees. The event broke the record for a non-Vegas residency, grossing $240 million USD over just 10 shows and injecting half a billion euros into Munich's economy that month. "They created Adele World, a place where she could perform twice a week for a month."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

facts.title: Knockout Blow Diss Track
facts.body: Released in early May 2024, this "fiendishly catchy single" was considered the "knockout blow" in Kendrick Lamar's beef with Drake. Its title "asserted Drake's outsider status in the hip-hop tradition," combining "headspinning lyrics and a juicy hook." "Kendrick deployed the knockout blow, a fiendishly catchy single called Not Like Us, a title that asserted Drake's outsider status in the hip-hop tradition."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Not Like Us

facts.title: Controversial Accusations
facts.body: In "Not Like Us," Kendrick Lamar made "pretty provocative accusations at Drake," including "accusing another artist of being both a colonizer in hip-hop culture and a pedophile." Despite the controversial nature of these allegations, the song became an "instant smash," defying typical pop music conventions. "Songs accusing another artist of being both a colonizer in hip-hop culture and a pedophile don't normally make for mass appeal pop music, but Not Like Us was an instant smash."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Not Like Us

facts.title: Epic Chart Run & Multiple Number Ones
facts.body: "Not Like Us" debuted at number one on the Hot 100 in mid-May 2024 and had an "epic chart run," spending "more than a year on the big chart, 53 weeks total, most of them in the top twenty." It returned to the number one spot two additional times, making it an unprecedented success for a diss track. "In Mid May, Not Like Us debuted at number one on the Hot 100 and began an epic chart run."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Not Like Us

facts.title: Music Video & Mainstream Visibility
facts.body: The "Not Like Us" music video was released in mid-July 2024. The song then took a "victory lap in two televised palaces of mainstream American culture" in February 2025, returning to number one on the Hot 100 after these high-profile appearances, further cementing its cultural impact. "after Lamar dropped the playfall Not Like Us music video and the following February, right after the song took a victory lap in two televised palaces of mainstream American culture."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Not Like Us

facts.title: Five Grammy Awards (2025)
facts.body: On February 2nd, 2025, "Not Like Us" won an astounding "five Grammys at the 67th annual Grammy Awards," including both Record of the Year and Song of the Year. This was "unprecedented" for a rap song, let alone a diss track, marking a historic moment for the genre's recognition in mainstream awards. "On February 2nd, 2025, on the 67th annual Grammy Awards Not Like Us won five Grammys, including both record and song of the year."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: Kanye West's Malibu Bomb Shelter Renovation (2024) – $57 Million Mansion Gutted
facts.body: Kanye West owned a house in Malibu and ordered its project manager to remove all windows, all electrical, and all plumbing to turn the $57 million mansion into a World War One–style bomb shelter. The project manager refused, citing safety, and was fired. "He ordered a project manager to remove all the windows, all the electrical and all the plumbing."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Flavor Flav Saved Red Lobster (2024)
facts.body: When Red Lobster faced financial ruin in 2024, Public Enemy's Flavor Flav — a huge Red Lobster fan — launched a public campaign to save the chain, and was largely successful. "He launched a crusade to save the chain."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Chechnya Banned Music Outside 80–115 BPM by Government Decree (2024)
facts.body: In April 2024, the Chechen government decreed that all music played in the republic must fall between 80 and 115 beats per minute, to ensure that musical and dance creations "align with the Chechen mentality and musical rhythm." All music too fast or too slow was banned. "All music in Chechnya must fall within between 80 and 115 beats per minute."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Aaron Jablonski's Bar Incident (March 16, 2024)
facts.body: In the early hours of March 16, 2024, Aaron Jablonski entered the Overtime Sports Bar in Clearwater, Florida, to find the karaoke machine broken. Enraged, he left, and when someone tried to calm him, he pulled out a 9-millimeter Glock pistol, waved it, and fired at least one shot, leading to charges of aggravated assault and felon in possession of a firearm. "In the early morning hours of March 16, 2024, police say that Aaron Jablonski walked into the overtime sports bar in Clearwater."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Record-Breaking Temporary Residency (Munich, 2024)
facts.body: In 2024, Live Nation constructed "Adele World," a temporary pop-up stadium in Munich with an 80,000-person capacity, specifically for Adele's residency. Over a month, she performed twice weekly to 730,000 attendees across 10 shows, setting a new record for a non-Vegas residency by grossing $240 million USD and bringing half a billion euros into the city. "They created Adele World, a place where she could perform twice a week for a month."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Ethical and Legal Debates on AI Voice Cloning (Early 2024)
facts.body: The rise of AI-generated music employing cloned voices and styles of existing artists has ignited significant moral, ethical, and legal controversies. As of early 2024, legal frameworks are struggling to keep pace with the rapid technological advancements, raising critical questions about unauthorized voice usage, intellectual property, and fair compensation for artists whose work informs AI models. "As of early 2024 this is a case where the law lags behind the technology."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History and Future of AI in Music

facts.title: No AI Fraud Act Introduction (January 10, 2024)
facts.body: On January 10, 2024, a group of US politicians introduced the No AI Fraud Act (No AI Fake Replicas and Unauthorized Duplications Act). This legislation specifically targets abusive deep fakes, voice clones, and exploitive digital impersonations created by AI, aiming to establish legal safeguards against the misuse of AI technology in artistic contexts. "On January 10th, 2024, a group of US politicians introduced the No AI Fraud Act."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History and Future of AI in Music

facts.title: National Recording Registry (2024)
facts.body: Blondie's album *Parallel Lines* was selected for preservation in the National Recording Registry by the Library of Congress in 2024. This honor is bestowed upon recordings deemed "culturally historically or aesthetically significant." "In 2024, Parallel Lines was selected for preservation in the national recording registry by the Library of Congress for being culturally historically or aesthetically significant."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s
facts.episode: Ep. 57 - Punk and New Wave at New York's CBGB

facts.title: Collaborative Resolution of Beef - Charli XCX & Lorde (2024)
facts.body: The collaboration between Charli XCX and Lorde on a remix of "Girl So Confusing" demonstrated "a new way a beef could go," offering a positive alternative to destructive feuds or legal battles. Lorde's verse, confessing insecurities that echoed Charli's, led to a successful dance hit and showed it's possible "to actually resolve your differences together on wax." "More important, it showed a new way a beef could go."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.body: The "song of the summer meme" experienced a notable comeback in 2024, driven by the latest hits from artists such as Post Malone, Morgan Wallen, Kendrick Lamar, Shaboozey, and Sabrina Carpenter. "Nonetheless, I am pleased that the song of the summer meme has made a comeback in 2024."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
